summary: The lecture covers the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, its definitions by scholars, historical evolution via the Objectives Resolution (1946-47), Supreme Court rulings on amendability (Berubari, Kesavananda Bharati, Bommai, LIC), the 42nd Amendment (1976) adding Socialist, Secular, Integrity, and explanations of key terms like Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic with their origins and types of democracy.
points: Ernest Barker called Preamble 'Key to the Constitution'; shortcut: Barker → Box key
N.A. Palkhivala termed Preamble 'Identity Card of Constitution'; shortcut: Palkhivala → Pal card
K.M. Munshi described Preamble as 'Horoscope of sovereign democratic republic'
Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru on Dec 13, 1946; adopted Jan 22, 1947; its 5th clause formed basis of Fundamental Rights
Berubari Union case (1960): Preamble not part of Constitution, cannot be amended
Kesavananda Bharati case (1973): Preamble is part of Constitution, amendable but basic structure unalterable
42nd Amendment (1976) by Indira Gandhi added Socialist, Secular, Integrity; only Preamble amendment so far
Correct Preamble order: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic
Sovereign defined by Jean Bodin (father of modern sovereignty) – independent decision-making
Socialism term first used by Robert Owen (father of cooperatives); Laski: 'manner of action'
Democracy originated in Greece (demos + kratos); Direct: Switzerland; Indirect: Parliamentary (India, UK) & Presidential (USA, Canada)
International Day of Democracy: Sept 15 (UN 2007); First women's suffrage: New Zealand (1893)
Liberty, Equality, Fraternity derived from French Revolution (1789)

check.q: Which Supreme Court case held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution but its basic structure cannot be amended?
Which amendment added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble?
Who described the Preamble as the 'Identity Card of the Constitution'?
